The design pass

14 candidate families · 56 front-view diagrams · four tasks per family. Hair and footwear are included in every full-body study.

Status

All new designs are directions. Existing uniform rules carry forward as constraints. Service wear is a possible civic or military role.

01 · How to read this workshop

Take away the emblem.
Can you still tell?

We compare the body’s outline first: a cropped jacket, an expanding robe, a wrapped waist, a rectangular mantle, a soft horizon or a working apron.

The controlled drawings

The front diagrams hold figure scale and pose constant. Grey tone distinguishes layers; school colours come later. Seams, panels and closures are schematic.

The illustrated trials

The two generated sheets explore how drape and posture feel on the body. Route A depicts everyday wear. Route B explores ceremonial extensions and alternative cuts. For a same-occasion comparison, use the controlled diagrams.

Hair shown on an individual figure is one styling choice. Each wardrobe accommodates different bodies, genders, hair textures and religious practices. The school’s identity belongs to its clothing operations.

Already visible in the first sheet: Temenggong’s wrap is a strong marker; Lan Fang’s cropped-over-long proportion separates it from TKI; Kora needs soft volume without ceremonial clutter. Merikani, Nine Rain and Sund need particular attention so that pale, useful clothing does not converge into one generic workwear style.

Detail checks remain: a renderer may turn a narrow band into a broad sash, move a cuff tab or expose too much heirloom lining. The exact diagram and written constraint take priority over an attractive accidental detail.

03 · Controlled comparison

The same task,
seven different answers.

Switch between routes and occasions. “Your mix” uses the per-school choices below.

Service diagrams explore task-ready clothing and do not depict protective equipment as if already certified. Sport diagrams are general movement studies; rowing, swimming and contact sport will need separate kits.

04 · Assignment boards

Four wardrobes
within each family.

Two candidate constructions per school, each carried through ceremony, everyday wear, movement and field service. The route is a design hypothesis; a final wardrobe can combine useful decisions from both.

01 · Parallax

Toa Keng Institution

What becomes visible when the body changes its frame?

A review note.

Inherited written constraint
Tropical worsted; four buttons; a disputed tie; Founding Day silt-dyed sash. Earlier material atlas also imagines long tropical field-scholar jackets.

A preserves the existing four-button blazer most directly. B tests a longer line against it, with the sash or stole offset.

Route A · construction

The chartered jacket

Chartered field scholar: a long, vented coat over a light base; institutional asymmetry expressed through pocket and closure placement.

Route B · construction

The field-scholar coat

Ceremonial drape: an additional offset stole over the established jacket. Keep the sash legible; do not turn it into an unrelated toga.

Hair / headwear

Open policy, secured clear of instruments during work. A ceremonial frame clip can hold hair of any texture.

Feet / ground

Quiet everyday lace-up or slip-on; terrain-specific field shoes; sport-specific soles. Boots by choice.

Working recommendation
A as the everyday baseline; B for ceremonial and field development.

02 · Amanah

Al-Merikani College

What must be shown, and what is held in trust?

A review note.

Inherited written constraint
Unstructured linen jacket and cotton overshirt; outward restraint; handwoven heirloom lining disclosed at a first contract. Indigo, ivory and brass are prior palette cues.

A keeps Merikani’s outward restraint in a straight open layer. B expands the lower volume through overlap and flare, keeping wealth inside.

Route A · construction

The inward treasury

Inward treasury: a clean long jacket whose precious woven facing appears only through an intentional gesture.

Route B · construction

The entrusted robe

Maritime robe: a lighter overlapping coat with a controlled flare, referencing kaftan and jama construction as separate studies.

Hair / headwear

Several documented wrapping and uncovered-hair options, chosen by wearer and community.

Feet / ground

Refined low-profile everyday shoe; grip footwear for decks; formal slip-on held securely during movement.

Working recommendation
A for everyday; develop B as a restrained ceremonial alternative.

03 · Communion

Sri Temenggong Institution

What responsibility can the body carry without displaying conquest?

A review note.

Inherited written constraint
Woven kain over trousers, learned tying method, tumpal border carrying responsibility; shoes removed at Balai Lama. Text currently both rejects visible rank and describes rank in the border.

Both preserve kain over trousers. A expresses competence through the wrap. B adds a shoulder plane and a longer upper line.

Route A · construction

The custodian’s wrap

Custodian’s wrap: spacious upper garment, kain, visible fold logic and a restrained shoulder cloth.

Route B · construction

The pavilion drape

Pavilion formality: longer upper line with greater drape, avoiding the assumption that pomp or gold equals authority.

Hair / headwear

Secure buns, braids, short hair and suitable coverings coexist. A court headdress belongs to a named ceremony.

Feet / ground

Established: shoes off at Balai Lama. Elsewhere: removable sandals or closed field shoes chosen for terrain; barefoot is situational.

Working recommendation
A for daily movement; B for ceremonies with entrusted cloth.

04 · Recomposition

Lan Fang College · 兰芳书院

How can a garment honour its inheritance while visibly revising it?

A review note.

Inherited written constraint
Uniform redesigned by a student committee every twenty years; nine versions; cohort date at cuff. Scholar tailoring and asymmetrical closures appear in Atlas III.

A contrasts a cropped jacket with a long shirt. B makes the split long line primary. These could be rival cohort designs, both alive at once.

Route A · construction

The edited scholar

Edited scholar: asymmetrical short jacket over a long split shirt; visible seam revisions and dated cuff.

Route B · construction

The split-line reformer

Archive of cohorts: retain two deliberately different generation silhouettes, so institutional time appears in a group portrait.

Hair / headwear

Style varies by cohort and individual, free of any single historical haircut.

Feet / ground

Distinctive sharp everyday shoe with practical walking version; athletics and workshop tasks use purpose-built footwear.

Working recommendation
Develop both as different dated cohorts before choosing a present-day baseline.

05 · Reciprocity

House of Nine Rain

Can what is worn account for what has been used?

A review note.

Inherited written constraint
Undyed heavy cotton cut for work; woven shoulder band records the cohort’s water and nutrient figures; contrasting repairs remain visible.

A keeps the work tunic dominant. B introduces a rectangular shoulder plane, while the ecological band and visible repairs stay readable.

Route A · construction

The woven ledger

Woven ledger: rectangular work tunic and divided lower layer; data band integrated into its construction.

Route B · construction

The seasonal mantle

Amphibious wrap: compact, replaceable panels with drying pathways, tested against the existing heavy-cotton rule.

Hair / headwear

Held clear of water, tools and measurement devices; the tying method can become a local house skill.

Feet / ground

Barefoot in chosen clean controlled spaces; wetland work uses protection suited to the actual terrain.

Working recommendation
A for the workday; B as a removable ceremonial layer.

06 · Third Voice

Sané-Kora Institute

How can the body be expressive without interrupting another voice?

A review note.

Inherited written constraint
Cloth is judged acoustically; no rustle, hard soles or clicking jewellery. Colour otherwise unregulated. Earlier atlas emphasises layered wraps and dress as speech.

A spreads softness across the shoulder. B gathers it into a more vertical pleated body. Both must pass the same acoustic rules.

Route A · construction

The quiet horizon

Quiet volume: a wide soft outer layer whose folds frame the speaker but do not announce movement.

Route B · construction

The pleated testimony

Pleated testimony: narrow pleats and a removable shoulder panel; each sample tested for sound as well as appearance.

Hair / headwear

Natural textures, braids, locs, short cuts and coverings accommodated. Headwrap and hairstyle are separate design categories.

Feet / ground

Established: soft soles only. Soft everyday soles with task-specific protective alternatives tested for noise.

Working recommendation
Keep both in the approved wardrobe family; test fabric sound before narrowing.

07 · Commons

The Sund Commons

Can a garment belong to many bodies across time?

A review note.

Inherited written constraint
Standard issue with generous seams, deep hems and long-compatible buttons; a linen tab records previous wearers. Earlier atlas’s northern wool-and-boots imagery needs tropical interpretation.

A communicates adjustability and succession. B makes maintenance and shared labour visible through a removable apron/vest.

Route A · construction

The shared jacket

Shared workwear: adjustable jacket and straight divided lower layer; spare cloth concentrated where growth and repair require it.

Route B · construction

The collective apron

Collective ceremony: same base, better maintained and joined by a shared woven shoulder piece; formality through care and assembly.

Hair / headwear

Haircut carries no rank. Secure hair for workshop tasks; head coverings compatible with protective equipment.

Feet / ground

Repairable everyday shoes; workshop protection where required. Northern boots stay a climate-specific option.

Working recommendation
A as daily base; B for workshop and civic service, with formality expressed through care.

05 · What the front view cannot settle

Draw the action
that could break the garment.

The next drawing pass needs back and side views, fastener sequences and moving bodies. These tests make the construction questions specific before a finished render makes them easy to overlook.

SchoolMovement or construction testWhat must survive
TKISeated writing, reaching across a laboratory bench, walking through rain. Compare short blazer against long coat from the side.Pocket access; tie storage during activity; vents that do not split the sash or create a catching loop.
MerikaniOpening and closing the front while stepping, boarding a vessel, revealing the lining by one deliberate gesture.The lining stays mostly inward. Flare must not pull the overlap open or make an unsecured trailing edge.
TemenggongFloor sitting, kneeling, large steps and removing footwear at the Balai Lama. Record the tying sequence from behind.The wrap remains secure over trousers. The border stays legible without turning duty into conspicuous rank.
Lan FangArms overhead, sitting, cycling and replacing a panel. Compare two cohort versions in rear view.The cropped-over-long relationship or split line survives movement. The date tab and revision seam stay in defined locations.
Nine RainSquatting to measure water, carrying tools, repeated wetting and drying; shoulder-band attachment under load.The band remains readable; repairs are visible; the heavy-cotton constraint is evaluated honestly before material revision.
KoraTurn, sit, gesture and walk across timber and stone. Record fabric and sole sound as separate samples.Soft volume does not drag, snag or rustle. Quiet wear must not prevent an intentional warning when needed.
SundTransfer one garment between different bodies; lengthen a hem; change a sleeve; carry workshop tools.Standard buttons, generous allowances and the wearer tab remain useful. Alterations allow each garment to pass to its next wearer.

The illustrations do not prove those tests pass. Back/side studies, pattern work and real material handling remain necessary. The magical layer should eventually make a wearing operation meaningful—fastening, entrusting, unfolding, exchanging, listening or sharing.

06 · My working judgement

What I would carry forward.

Keep distinctions in proportion.

TKI is articulated and institutionally contained. Lan Fang’s short-over-long or split construction visibly revises that containment. Merikani has continuous length and controlled disclosure. Keep these differences strong before adding more patterns.

Give the waist two different jobs.

Temenggong’s wrap is a practised act of custodianship. Nine Rain’s material record belongs to making, repair and measured exchange. A decorative sash on each would erase that difference.

Kora needs a wardrobe.

The horizon and the pleated column can both satisfy the acoustic rule. Allowing both may express the school more faithfully than forcing a uniform silhouette. The present monochrome study does not revoke its freedom of colour.

Sund’s ceremony is maintenance.

I would keep its best-maintained shared garment as formal wear. The apron/vest earns a place through workshop and civic use. A grand ceremonial cloak would need a stronger reason than visual parity with the others.

Most promising first family: TKI A/B by occasion; Merikani A with B ceremony; Temenggong A with B entrusted drape; Lan Fang as two dated cohorts; Nine Rain A with a removable B mantle; Kora as an acoustically approved range; Sund A plus the working B apron.

This is my recommendation for the next pass. Your saved choices remain independent of it.

07 · Review record

Keep the choices,
including the unfinished ones.

Selections are saved in this browser when local storage is available. Export a JSON record to carry them into the next pass or send them back here. “Hybrid” means the two constructions are developed together; the comparison shows route A as a visual stand-in until that hybrid is drawn.

The next image pass

Develop the chosen garment families into front, side and back character sheets; resolve fasteners, shoes and hair options; then produce colour and material variants. Finished JPG/PNG editorial plates follow the construction decisions we keep here.

08 · Provenance

What belongs to which layer.

Inherited fiction: school identities and clothing rules from the existing Great Schools material chapters, carried forward in Dress Atlas I.

New design directions: all route A/B constructions, diagrammatic placements, garment variations and the working recommendations in this volume.

Historical analogues: the referenced costume research remains in Part I. This workshop makes no new claims about real-world national dress, direct cultural descent or decoded historical textile meanings.

Visuals: original SVG construction diagrams plus two graphite-style costume illustrations made with the built-in image-generation tool, following the written brief.

The downloadable package includes the diagram boards as editable SVG and rendered PNG, comparison sheets, the two original generated PNGs, and a brief explaining the design status and review process. The HTML embeds its images and diagrams for offline reading; no website has been modified.
